turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Good morning, Mrs.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Turner.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Can you tell me your full name and your birthday?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Odessa Turner. April 19th,

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I'm 91 years old, and I still remember it, so don't you worry. Sharpe as ever.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Did Gloria bring you today?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: She did. She's out in the waiting room on her phone. She's the one who made me come. Well, I'm glad she did.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: What's been going on? I'm just worn out, doctor, for about six weeks now.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I nap in the morning and again, after the day. lunch and I used to never nap. My tomatoes are going to waste because I can't get out to the garden.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: That's a big change for you, any dizziness.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: When I first get up out of bed in the morning, the room kind of swims for a second. Then it passes.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Have you fallen at all? No,

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I hold on to the dresser.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Any chest pain or shortness of breath?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No chest pain,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: I breathe fine. fever, black stools, or losing weight without trying.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No, none of that.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Have you been feeling down or sad?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No, I'm not sad, just tired.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Let's go through your pills. I have amla -depine 5 mg once a day for your blood pressure, Metaprolol 50 mg twice a day,

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Adorvastatin 10 at night, and a baby aspirin,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: 81 mg.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Anything else?

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: That's right,

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: and I take a Tylenol PM at bedtime because I wasn't sleeping.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Every night.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Oh, and I quit the vitamin D. Those pills are too big to swallow. Okay, that's helpful.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Any other new problems this year?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Well, I had pneumonia last winter, but I got over that. Lungs have been fine since.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Good. Let me check you. Sitting your blood pressure is 118 over 64, and your pulse is 52, which is on the slow side. standing up, the pressure drops to 104 over 60. Your heart is slow but regular,

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: no murmur,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: lungs are clear, no swelling in your ankles, your color looks good, no paleness inside the eyelids. We also did an ECG while you were waiting. It shows a slow regular rhythm, a rate of 52, and no heart block.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: So what's making me so tired?

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: I think a big part is your medicines. Your pulse is slow and the metroprolol may be slowing it too much, And the Tylenol PM has different hydromine in it, which is a sleepy antihistamine.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: At 91,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: it can make you drowsy all day.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: My goodness, I thought it was just the Tylenol.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: A lot of people think that, so here's the plan. Stop the Tylenol PM. If you have aches at night, plain Tylenol, that's acetaminophen 500mg is fine. Cut the metaprolol down to 25mg twice a day, that's half a tablet. Keep the amla -depine, adorvastatin and aspirin the same. What about sleeping then? Same bedtime every night, no long afternoon naps and some light in the morning. That helps more than you'd think. For the vitamin D, I'll switch you to a chewable 1 ,000 units a day.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: A chewable I can do.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: I also want some blood work today.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: A blood count,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: chemistry panel, thyroid test and B12 to make sure we're not missing anything else.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: All right.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Get up slowly, sit on the edge of the bed for a minute first. First, if you faint, have chest pain or your pulse gets slower, call us or go to the emergency

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: room.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: I'll see you in two weeks and we'll call Gloria at 555 -0177 with the results.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: That's her number. Thank you doctor. I'll bring you some tomatoes if I get my energy back. I'll hold you to that Mrs. Turner.
